On X11, read the per-monitor work areas from `_GTK_WORKAREAS_D0` (published by mutter/GNOME) and fall back to `_NET_WORKAREA` only when it's not available. GTK and Wine do the same.

## What is the current behavior?
`_NET_WORKAREA` is a single rectangle for the whole desktop. Intersecting it with each monitor gives wrong working areas when the monitors aren't edge-aligned. `ManagedPopupPositioner` clamps popups to that area, so menus open in the wrong place: shifted right in #21956, and too low on a taller monitor next to a shorter, bottom-aligned primary in https://github.com/SubtitleEdit/subtitleedit/issues/15947.

## What is the updated/expected behavior with this PR?
Each monitor gets its own working area from `_GTK_WORKAREAS_D0` (the rect contained in its bounds). Window managers without that property behave as before.

Builds; not tested on a real multi-monitor X11 setup.

## Fixed issues
Fixes #21956
